About Me

A builder who thinks
in systems.

I'm Benjamin Umeh, a Product Manager with a BSc in Computer Science. My technical foundation gives me an edge most PMs lack I understand the systems behind the products I manage.

I've owned the full product lifecycle across three products Outbound AI, FitCall.me, and DEPATH — driving everything from PRD creation and pricing strategy to design coordination and cross-team execution. My work on Outbound AI earned commendation from senior mentors, and FitCall.me is currently in active build with me leading the product. Most recently, I founded DEPATH, a Nigeria-first route safety platform, where I owned product strategy, verification architecture, and AI workflow design end-to-end — including running a full codebase audit that caught a data-fabrication risk before a single user saw it.

My approach is rooted in user empathy, structured documentation, and the ability to communicate clearly across engineering, design, and business stakeholders. I adapt fast, collaborate well, and ship.

Products I've
built & owned.

01
DEPATH Founder & Product Manager Pre-launch MVP
Founder and Product Manager for DEPATH, a Nigeria-first route safety platform — a pre-travel decision layer that checks a route before you open your navigation app, not after. Owned product strategy, product discovery, UX design, verification architecture, AI workflow design, branding, and technical direction. Set the rule that no incident reaches the public map without a media cross-reference, and scoped go-to-market around seven named transport corridors instead of a national launch. Ran a full codebase audit on the build and caught a data-fabrication risk in the route analyzer before a single user saw it.

AdaptPulse Founder & Product Lead Design Stage
Founder and Product Lead for AdaptPulse, a simulation-based adaptability training concept built as a diagnostic simulation rather than edtech. Locked the product vocabulary as Case, Reading, and Debrief, and narrowed V1 scope to a single simulation and one persona, with no numeric scoring and no employer-facing features. Designed the full brand identity, the Fault Line mark, an Ink, Parchment, Brass, Signal, and Alert palette, and a type system pairing Newsreader italic with IBM Plex Sans and IBM Plex Mono, and wrote the build prompt for Google AI Studio.

FitCall.me Product Manager In Build
Served as Product Manager for FitCall.me a virtual fitness platform connecting US and UK clients with vetted Nigerian personal trainers via scheduled one-on-one video sessions. Authored the full PRD (v0.1), milestone documentation across 6 phased build cycles, and versioning records. Played a pivotal role in solidifying product direction including scoping MVP features, defining what was in and out of scope, and guiding critical trade-off decisions during key moments in the build phase.

Learnings

Key lessons from
real projects.

01 DESIGN ACCURACY
Alignment is a product decision
No matter how polished a design looks, poor alignment creates friction in development. Now I review every design with a builder's eye making sure what looks good can also be built properly.
02 PRODUCT UNDERSTANDING
Know the product before you manage it
Shallow product knowledge produces shallow tickets and weak decisions. I make it a point to understand every product I manage thoroughly from how it's built to how users move through it before making calls.
03 RESEARCH OVER SHORTCUTS
The best insights come from within
AI tools can assist, but genuine product intuition comes from real research and deep product understanding. I've learned to go deeper before reaching for shortcuts the results are always stronger.
04 CONFIDENCE & CLARITY
Confidence accelerates delivery
Approaching tasks with confidence rather than hesitation produces better work, faster and earns more trust from teams and stakeholders. Being clear when you speak is just as important as being clear in how you think.
